AUTHOR: Böer
TITLE: Segmentation of Fish in Realistic Underwater Scenes using Lightweight Deep Learning Models
VENUE: Proceedings of ROBOVIS 2021 (2nd International Conference on Robotics, Computer Vision and Intelligent Systems)
REGION: North Sea (~45 nmi west of Sylt, 22 m) and Kiel Fjord (Baltic Sea), Germany
DATA: Own stationary seafloor sensor platform stereo video (monochrome low-light cameras); 600 labeled images + 1148-image test set from a different day
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'made it possible to record without active lighting from dawn to dusk, which was verified to a maximum depth of 22m.'
D2: 600 images random 80/10/10; separate independent test set of 1148 images recorded on a different day
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'very similar samples may appear in the test and training set ... a separate test set of 1148 images, that where recorded on a different day'
R_EV: Sec. 4.3: 'The performance of each model on the independent test set of 1148 images' (different day, same platform/campaign; P2 -> not external)
C_EV: Sec. 4.2: 'All segmentation results were thresholded at a confidence value of 0.5 to obtain binary masks.' (segmentation-only, no detection/counting output)
E_EV: Table 1: 'Average pixel level accuracy and IoU as obtained by the two utilized models.' (length/biomass only planned as future work)
ARCH: PSPNet and DeepLabv3 with MobileNetV2 encoder (pruned, lightweight)
METR: Pixel accuracy, IoU, inference FPS, model size
NOTE: Main split is random image-level 80/10/10 with leakage explicitly acknowledged; an additional test set from a different recording day is the reported evaluation -> D1 coded 조사일. Under P2 the different-day test is within the same campaign, so R1=N. Visibility: depth (22 m) and passive/low-light illumination reported; 'difficult visibility conditions' only qualitative; failure cases (twilight, poor lower-image illumination) discussed qualitatively, no stratified metrics -> V6=N. Binary segmentation only, no counting -> C_ALL=NA. ENV coded NR because it is not stated whether the annotated images come from the North Sea or Kiel Fjord deployment (temperate seafloor). FPS=Y (cameras up to 20 frames/s).
